facts.text: Sand Hill developed as a rural community after Oklahoma became a state in 1907, following the allotment of Creek Nation lands.
The community of Sand Hill is situated southeast of Muskogee and is bordered by the Arkansas River to the north.
Early settlers in Sand Hill were primarily farmers drawn to the fertile river bottoms along the Arkansas and Verdigris rivers.
Sand Hill's founding economy centered on agriculture, with cotton as a dominant cash crop alongside corn, wheat, and beef cattle.
Local production in Sand Hill was supported by cotton gins and grain mills, utilizing the area's sandy soils for mixed farming.
Agricultural mechanization, including spindle cotton pickers and improved tractors, led to a significant decline in Sand Hill after World War II.
